verdict.justification: B is the stronger operational planning deliverable because it combines a more maintainable spreadsheet with a better-protected recovery scenario. Both correctly include May’s quantities despite the source total omitting them, preserve the customer’s production sequence, and conclude that only Scenario 3 meets both shipment deadlines. B deliberately schedules the four-week extended-day window for “Tue 20-Feb to Mon 19-Mar,” obtaining 20 production days rather than A’s 19 and adding 35 sets of useful contingency. B also quantifies the resulting buffers—45 sets before the April deadline and 190 sets through April—rather than relying mainly on A’s whole-working-day descriptions of float. Its scenario sheets calculate production allocations from centralized inputs and show cumulative demand, production, remaining orders, and variance, whereas A explicitly makes daily production quantities manual “plan inputs.” A offers finer individual-PO tracking and a more concise written summary, but B’s live comparison, explicit sensitivities, and actionable transfer and staffing contingencies make it preferable for the operations meeting and subsequent daily management.

decisive_issues.issue: Optimizes the temporary extended-day window to avoid losing an enhanced-capacity day to a holiday.
decisive_issues.quote: The window starts the day after Louis Riel Day, so all 20 extended days are production days (+700 sets).
